OBITUARY REFERENCE 
MR. CHAIRMAN: I refer with profound sorrow to the passing away of 
Maulana Habibur Rahman Nomani, a former Member of this House on the 17th 
August, 2005 at the age of 79 years. 
Maulana Habibur Rahman Nomani was born in Village Imam Ganj, 
Maunath Bhanjan, Uttar Pradesh in August, 1926 and had his education at his 
native place in the Jamia Miftahul Oloom. 
A social and political worker, Maulana Habibur Rahman actively 
participated in the Quit India Movement. Maulana Nomani started 
educational programme and taught children and youth at Imam Ganj. He also 
took keen interest in solving the problems of weavers and artisans. He stood for 
secular values. Way back in 1950, he organised agitation against landlords 
compelling them to give land back to the Dalits and Harijans. Maulana 
Nomani was also associated with va rious social, welfare and educational 
organisations. He was Chairman of the Etawah Cotton Spinning Mill, Uttar 
Pradesh and also served as the Chairman of the U.P Minority and Backward 
Class Federation. 
Maulana Nomani started his legislativ e career with memb ership of Uttar 
Pradesh Legislative Assembly, where he was a Member from 1969 to 1974. 
He was also elected to the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council in 1975 and 
remained a member of that Council till 1980. He also served as Deputy Minister 
in the Government of Uttar Pradesh from 1970 to 1972 and Minister of State 
from 1976 to 1977. 
Maulana Habibur Rahman Nomani was nominated to this House in 
August, 1993 and remained a Member till August, 1999. 
In the passing away of Maulana Habibur Rahman Nomani, the country has 
lost a veteran Parliamentarian and a noted social worker. 

RAJYASABHA [18 August, 2005] 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Maulana Habibur Rahman Nomani.

Expansion of UN Security Council 
*342. SHRI RAJ NATH SINGH: Will the Minister of EXTERNALAFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the latest position in relation to the expansion of the UN Security 
Council; 
(b) whether Government have been assured of full support from the P-5; 
(c) whether Government have been able to muster support in relation to this in 
the UN General Assembly; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI RAO INDERJIT SINGH): (a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the 
House. 
Statement 
(a) to (d) Government of India believe s that no reform of the UN will be 
complete without the reform and expansion of the UN Security Council. The 
Security Council must, in its composition, reflect contemporary geo-political 
realities and not those of 1945; its actions must be representative, legitimate and 
effective and its methods of work and decision making process more 
democratic, transparent and responsive.To reflect the 
4 

[18 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
changed realities, it is essential that the Security Council is expanded in both the 
permanent and non-permanent categor ies. The inclusion of developing 
categories. The inclusion of developing countries from Asia, Africa and Latin 
America, who are capable of global responsibility, will contribute to optimal 
decision making necessary to address the insecurity of developing countries. 
India's impeccable credentials for permanent membership of the UN 
Security Council are well known. It is clear and widely recognized that on the 
basis of any objective criteria such as the population, size, GDP, the economic 
potential, cultural diversity, civilizational legacy, maturity of political system, 
contribution to the activities of the UN, in particular to peace keeping 
operations, and its unique developing country perspective, India is well qualified to 
be a permanent member of the UN Security Council. 
Support for India's candidature for permanent membership of the UN 
Security Council has been expressed in various forms and fora. Some 
countries, have expressed support confidentially in bilateral discussions. There 
has been a steady accretion of support to India's candidature since it was 
announced in 1994. 
Any reform of the Un Security Council requires amendment of the UN 
Charter, which is complex exercise. India, along with Brazil, Japan and 
Germany-now being termed as the Group of Four (G-4) countries-have 
introduced a Framework Resolution which seeks to reform and restructure the UN 
Security Councit through a three step process, consisting of a decision on the 
Framework Resolution, the election of new permanent members in the General 
Assembly and subsequently, the adoption of a Resolution for revision of the UN 
Charter. All these steps require support of two-thirds majority of the entire UN 
membership. For entry into force of the Charter amendment, ratification by two- 
thirds majority of the entire UN membership including all the current 
permanent members of the UN Security Council is required. The G-4 countries 
have been actively engaging with other member countries of the UN to mobilize 
support in favour of their initiative. They have formally introduced the 
Framework Resolution in the General Assembly. The African Union (AU) as 
well as the Uniting for Consensus Group, formerly known as the 'Coffee Club', have 
also introduced their Resolutions in the UN General Assembly. 
5 

RAJYA SABHA [18 August, 2005] 
India and other countries of the G-4 have been actively engaged with the 
countries of the African Union with the objective of introducing a joint G4-AU 
Resolution. On the basis of the understanding reached between the G-4 and the 
African Union Follow-up Mechanism during discussions held in London on July 
25,2005, it was agreed that the latter would consult the African States and revert on 
harmonizing the G-4 and AU Resolutions and having a joint Resolution. While 
the African Union, at its Extraordinary Summit held in Addis Ababa on August 
4, 2005, could not endorse the London Understanding, further efforts in this 
direction are being made. 
Among the P-5 countries (China, France, the Russian Federation, the UK and 
the USA), France, Russia and the UK have publicly expressed support for 
India's candidature for permanent membership of the UN Security Council. France is 
a co-sponsor of the G-4 Resolution and the UK is also supportive of this. The 
India-US Joint Statement issued on July 18, 2005 during Prime Minister's visit 
to Washington DC, inter-alia, states that "international institutions must fully 
reflect changes in the global scenario that have taken place since 1945. The 
president (of the USA) reiterated his view that international institution are going 
to have to adapt to reflect India's central and growing role." As for China, the 
Joint Statement signed by the Prime Ministers of India China on April 11, 2005, 
during the latter's visit to India, inter-alia, states "The Chinese side also reiterated 
that India is an important developing country and is having an increasingly 
important influence in the international arena. China attaches great importance 
to the status of India in international affairs. It understands and supports India's 
aspirations to play an active role in the UN and international affairs."

science community.

received.

CBI raids against Civil Servants 
*351. DR. GYAN PRAKASH PILANIA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the number of I.A.S., LPS. and I.R.S. officers who have been raided by 
C.B.I. during last five years; 
(b) how many cases have been registered against these officers on the basis of 
these raids; 
(c) how many have been challanged out of above cases; 
(d) how many have been convicted out of challaned cases; 
(e) what conclusions Government draw from above statistics regarding 
corruption scenario in above elite services; and 
(f) what steps Government intend to take to improve the situation? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, 
PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRISURESH PACHOURI):(a) and 
(b) During 2000-04, CBI conductd searches in 185 cases after registration of 
cases under various sections of Prevention of Corruption Act and other criminal 
laws in respect of 48 IAS officers, 10 IPS officers and 127 IRS officers. 
(c) Charge sheets have been filed in the competent courts in 50 cases. 
(d) Two cases have resulted in conviction so far. 
(e) No definite trend is discernible from the above statistics. 
(f) Several steps have been taken in the past years in order to remove 
corruption and to improve administrative functioning. Important among these steps 
are: Enacting the Right to Information Act, 2005; Notification of the Whistle 
Blowers Resolution, 2004; the proactive involvement of Ministries/ Departments 
through Annual Action Plan on Vigilance; issue of comprehensive instructions 
on transparency in tendering and contracting processes by the CVC; enactment of 
CVC Act and, strengthening the CBI to discharge its anti-corruption work; 
increased use of Information and Communication Technology; introduction 
of Citizens Charters, and simplifications of procedures and systems etc.

Coal shortage 
*355. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to 
state:  
(a) whether there is an acute shortage of coal in the country at present; 
(b) if so, what steps Government propose to ensure that no wastage of the 
commodity takes place; 
(c) whether there is any proposal to import coal to tide over the situation; and 
(d) if so, the sources thereof and the likely cost per metric tonne at which 
it would be available in the country, including insurance and freight? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL (DR. DASARI 
NARAYAN RAO):(a)As per demand assessed by the Planning Commission for 
2005-06, the total raw coal demand would be 445.65 million tonnes whereas 
the total availability from indigenous sources is estimated at 406.48 million 
tonnes. This leaves a gap of 39.17 million tonnes. The shortage of coal in the 
country during 2005-06 is proposed to be met through imports by various 
sectors and also through additioal efforts for enhancement of domestic 
production. 
(b) Around 80% of coal produced by CIL is consumed by power sector. In 
order to prevent wastage, Ministry of Power has worked out consumptbn 
44 

[18 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
norms for power utilities. The norms are applied while deciding on allocation of coal 
to power generation units. Ministry of Power is also impressing upon coal 
consuming power utilities to improve their thermal efficiency so as to optimize 
coal consumption. Subsidiaries of Coal India are modernizing coal mining 
techniques by introducing latest technology to optimize production and 
reduce wastage. 
(c) Import of coal is not done centrally. Since coal is under Open General 
Licence (OGL), consumers are free to import coal based on their 
requirements. It is expected that the gap between indigenous supply and 
demand of coal during 2005-06 will be met to a large extent through import of 
coal by power, steel and cement sectors and other industries. 
(d) By and large, coal is imported by individual consumers from 
Indonesia, South Africa, Australia and China, to supplement indigenous 
supplies. The landed cost of  imported coal will depend upon the negotiated 
cost with the vendor and also distance from pithead to unloading port.

Registration of Trade Unions 
†* 359. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether in view of the incident  of Gurgaon, Government are 
considering to make changes in the labour laws; 
(b) the details of the existing law regarding registration of 'trade unions', and 
the steps being taken by Government to make the registration mandatory; 
and 
(c) whether Government have any information about the number of trade unions 
of the employees working in multinational companies? 
THE MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT (SHRI K. 
CHANDRA SHEKHAR RAO): (a) to (c) Review of labour laws is a 
continuous process. Amendments are proposed after detailed consultation with the 
social partners with a view to harmonize the interests of all the stakeholders. 
The Trade Unions Act, 1926 provides for mode of registration of trade unions 
under the Act. No trade union of workme n shall be registered unless at least 
10 per cent of 100, whichever is less, subject to a minimum of seven 
workmen engaged or employed in the establishment or industry with which it 
is connected are the members of such trade unions on the date of making of 
application for registration. The Trade Unions Act was last amended in 2001. 
At present, there is no proposal to further amend the Act to make the 
registration of trade unions mandatory. 
The Trade Unions Act, 1926, is administered by the State Governments. The 
information about the number of trade unions of the employees working in 
multinational companies is not centrally maintained. 
Outsourcing of Research and Development 
*360.   SHRI MOOLCHAND MEENA: DR. 
T SUBBARAMI REDDY: 
Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi.  
65 

RAJYA SABHA [18 August, 2005] 
(a) whether the integration of India and China into global economy and 
consequent increase in outsourcing of research and development to these nations 
have not only made revolutionary impact on the cost of drug development in 
west but also helped reshape domestic industries in both the nations; 
(b) whether as per the recent findin gs in the 19th Annual Global 
Biotechnology report, India and Chin a are improving their regulatory 
systems; and 
(c) to what extent both countries have agreed to play a greater role in 
Biotechnology? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) to  (c) Sir, with ever-increasing 
cost of drug development in the West, it has become difficult for companies 
to sell drugs based on the cost of Re search and Development and clinical 
trials. The pharmaceuticals companies ha ve to recover the cost of drug 
discovery and, therefore, have to price the drugs at levels, which are 
unaffordable even to the middle class in USA and Europe. Also it is a burden 
on the state exchequer due to the increas ing cost of social security benefits. 
Spiralling costs in R&D and drug development have made USA and European 
countries look towards outsourcing in India and China by establishing their 
R&D centers and conducting clinical trials in these countries. This provides a 
great opportunity for India. By lib eralizing the environment for such 
investments, they will have a positive impact on the domestic pharmaceutical 
industry. With Patent Act, 1970 in place and protection given to product 
patents Indian pharmaceuticals companies also have to compete and survive 
in the international market through innovations. India is already a large 
exporter of generics and more and more companies in India are investing in 
drug discovery and development. The revolutionary impact on nations 
outsourcing R&D, especially in India and China will be seen in the years to 
come depending on the response of the Indian Pharmaceutical companies and 
the opportunities available to large pharmaceuticals companies in the world with 
the ever-changing liberalized environment for partnerships with such 
companies both in India and China. 
India needs to change its regulatory framework to achieve efficiency, 
66 

[18 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
world-class standards for clinical trials and establish a professionalized multi-
disciplinary regulatory body dealing with contemporary biotech and pharma 
issues. With the new Biotech Development Strategy under discussion all the 
challenges including putting in place an effective regulatory system are sought to be 
met. The biotech industry has already achieved an annual turnover of $ 1 billion 
and destined to leap forward as a sizable section of the Industry is ready to meet 
the challenges of global competition required to be met pursuant to the 
amendments in 2005 and earlier amendment in 1970 the India Patent Act, 
including granting product protection. The large skilled human resource base 
available in India for which India is uniquely placed coupled with low cost economy 
can help shape the nature of domestic industry and pave the way for India to 
capture a larger market share of the global drug and biotech industry. The same 
logic with some variables also applies to China. As per the published Global 
Biotechnology Report 2004 "Beyond Borders", of Earnest and Young, both India 
and China are positioned to take advantage of moves by Governments in the US and 
Europe to create a regulatory framework for approving generic versions of successful 
protein drugs, whose patent is expiring in the near future.

88 

[18 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) if so, the total number of sites caught fire and since when the sites caught 
fire alongwith reasons therefor; 
(c) whether his Ministry has claimed that these fires would soon be 
brought under control; and 
(d) if so, the steps taken to extinguish these fires and prevent recurrence of fire 
in future? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL (DR. DASARI 
NARAYAN RAO): (a) and (b) It is a fact that some mines of Bharat Coking Coal 
Limited (BCCL) are having fires for decades. In BCCL, at the time of 
nationalization it was estimated that about 70 mine fires existed in 40 
collieries. These mine fires have been inherited by BCCL. The reasons for mine 
fires are unscientific mining before nationalization, inherent nature of coal of being 
susceptible to combustion, spreading of fires from adjoining localities, bush fire 
(ban tulsi) etc. In CCL, four fires are existing in 3 collieries for over a decade. 
The fires occurred due to spontaneous heating. 
(c) and (d) As a result of the efforts made, 10 fires of BCCL have been 
extinguished and the remaining fires are by and large kept under control. The 
following steps have been taken to control/extinguish and to prevent recurrence 
of fires in coal mines: 
(i) Sand flushing into active fire zone from surface to underground through 
boreholes. 
(ii) Surface blanketing to prevent breathing in of air to the fire area. 
(iii) Inert gas flushing from surface through boreholes to extinguish fire. 
(iv) Quenching of spot fire and mining out the quenched coal. 
(v) Sealing of the part of the mine under fire by construction of fire 
stoppings/isolation stoppings. 
(vi) Application of fire resistant sealant in and around the isolation 
stopping/fire stoppings. 
(vii) Regular monitoring with the help of Co-detectors, toximeter, air 
sampling and analysis of the same at colliery level. 
(viii) Trench cutting by mechanized means to excavate fire and to prevent spread 
of the same. 
89 

RAJYASABHA [18 August, 2005] 
(ix) Intentional flooding by water to quench the fire in some mines. 
Apart from above actions, 13 schemes for dealing with fires and control of 
subsidence in BCCL have been sanctioned and funded by the Government. 
Out of these, 7 schemes have been completed. A Master Plan has also been 
prepared to deal with fires and control of subsidence in Jharia coalfield as a long 
term measure. 
In CCL, various measures have been taken to extinguish and control the fire 
such as sealing off to cut oxygen supply, submerging with water, filling up with 
non-combustible material etc.

Revenue drop of BSNL 
2540. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA TAIMUR : Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a sharp dec lining of revenue of BSNL is about 
to 6,500 crores in the current financial year; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is a fact that BSNL's revenue drop due to its inability to take 
timely and market friendly decision; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and whether Government have initiated any action 
to control such huge revenue drop? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) No, 
Sir. During the first quarter of the current financial year, revenue of BSNL in basic 
services is less by Rs. 231 Crores as compared to the corresponding period of the 
last financial year.

RAJYASABHA [18 August, 2005] 
(b) Does not arise in view of (a) above. 
(c) No, Sir. 
(d) *    BSNL is having a comprehensive marketing strategy comprising 
of Annual visibility plan to get maximum visibility throughout the 
year on all mass media. 
* Franchisee policy has been laid down under which more than 1200 
franchisees along with their more than 15000 sub-franchisees 
will market the services of BSNL throughout the country. 
* Commercial procedures for all the services of BSNL have been 
simplified so that customers will have hassle free transaction across 
the counter. 
* Special promotional schemes are launched by BSNL during 
various cultural and religious festivals. 
TRAI's approvals for concessions 
2541 SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN: Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the fact that certain mobile phone 
companies such as Reliance India Mobile entice the people of free 
downloads and charge for such downloads later; 
(b) whether Government would direct the companies to honour their 
commitments in the interests of consumers; and 
(c) whether Government would make it mandatory to get the approval of TRAI 
before announcing/withdrawing any concession by mobile companies? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS 
AND INFORMATIONTECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) and (b) 
No, Sir. However, earlier a number of instances have come to the notice of Telecom 
Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), where customers were offered certain 
value added services free of charge by some cellular mobile phone 
operators/companies. Later on these free value added services were made 
chargeable and the customers were info rmed that if they do not want the 
service they should "unsubscribe" by sending SMS. To protect 
122 

[18 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
the interest of customers in this regard, TRAI on 03.05.2005 directed all 
Cellular Mobile Service Providers and Unified Access Service Providers that no 
chargeable value added service shall be provided to customer without his 
explicit consent. Any value added service, which was earlier being provided 
free of charge, shall not be made chargeable without the explicit consent of the 
customers. 
(c) No such proposal is under consideration at present. 
Scheme to increase the revenue 
†2542. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL APTE: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether any scheme is under the consideration of Indian Posts and 
Telegraph department to arise its revenue; 
(b) if so, whether any new scheme is proposed to be introduced to compete 
with courier services; 
(c) if so, the features of the new scheme; and 
(d) the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) to (d) 
To generate revenues, the Department of Posts has initiated a number of measures 
under Plan to modernize it and induct technology into its various operation. 
Approximately 79% of the Tenth Plan outlay of Rs. 1350 crores has been 
earmarked for this purpose. New Products and Services introduced recently are 
Logistics Post and Direct Post, with a view to generate revenue. Introduction of new 
products/services and refinement of existing products/ servies are a continuous 
process to compete with couriers. 
With Logistics Post, the Department is trying to build on its core 
competence and the reach of its network,  to offer a service that has been 
identified even at the international level, as an area of future growth for Postal 
systems. Logistics Post has been designed for transmission of consignment 
loads across the country. 
Direct Post deals with the processing and delivery of sales messages/

announcements as un-addressed mail. Direct Post is another business segment 
that has become a successful revenue stream in many Postal Systems. 
The existing products/services are system atically marketed by establishing 
a separate Marketing mechanism in the Business Development and Marketing 
Directorate as well as in all the States across the country. The Department is also 
seeking to optimally utilise the existing manpower by redeploying them to meet 
the emerging work requirement. 
Annual Spectrum Charges 
2543. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that TRAI recommended for lowering the ceiling of 
annual spectrum charges payable by service providers to Government from the 
existing 6 per cent to 4 per cent on annual gross revenue; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that  TRAI has also recommended for 
constitution of Group of Ministers; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) in what manner, Government are going to ensure availability of 
adequate spectrum to achieve the targ et of 20 million mobile subscribers by 
2007? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEELAHMAD): (a) Yes, 
Sir. 
(b) and (c) Yes, Sir. In para 3.9.3 of their recommendations on Spectrum Related 
Issues, the TRAI has recommended the following. 
"In view of the gravity of the situation in regard to spectrum availability for 
various operators even to the short term of 2007 to meet the targets set by the 
Government for Cellular telephones and at the same time the nearly insurmountable 
difficulties faced by Defence in vacating the spectrum in such a short time 
frame, we strongly recommend immediate constitution of a group at the level of 
Ministers of the Union Government assisted by professionals from Defence, 
Department of Telecom and TRAI to draw up 
124 

[18 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
a detailed time bound step-by-step programme and monitor its 
implementation. The mandate of the Group would have to include 
identification of alternative band, assessing and making available requisite funds 
and assisting users on procedural aspects of quick procurement and installation 
of new equipment. This activity has to be taken up on war footing to be able to 
meet the Government objectives of growth in telecom services." 
(d) Adequate spectrum to achieve the target of 200 million mobile 
subscribers by 2007 is sought to be made available including by release of 
necessary spectrum from existing users through coordination/relocation.

(c) whether the Prime Minister during the recent visit to England, last month 
raised the issue with British Prime Minister and impressed upon him to

160 

[18 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
and nuclear related end users in India, which exceeded the restrictions imposed by NSG.

2585. SHRI VEDPRAKASH P. GOYAL: Will the Minister of LABOUR 
AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:

(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT (SHRI K. 
CHANDRA SEKHAR RAO): (a) and (b) The Government enacted the Contract Labour 
(Regulation & Abolition) Act, 1970 with a view to have a check on hiring of contract 
labour and prevent their exploitation. It provides for prohibition of employment 
of contract labour, in circumstances like the work being of perennial nature etc.

core competencies etc. which, in their view, leads to cost effectiveness, and 
increase in efficiency and productivity.

outstanding as on 31.3.2005 are to be consolidated and rescheduled for 
repayment in 20 equal annual instalments at a reduced interest rate of 7.5%,

from 2005-06 to 2009-10 on the consolidated central loan, subject to laid down conditions.

guidelines called 'The States' Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility (DCRF) 2005-06 to

2614. SHRIMATI JAMANA DEVIBARUPAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be

income in 10 years time frame by 2012. It settled for a target growth of 8.1 percent during 
2002-03 to 2006-07, start with raising it further in the subsequent five years. 
(b) An eight per cent rate of growth was considered necessary for achieving the 
social and economic targets of the Tenth Plan. It could be achieved, inter- alia, by: (i) 
Making larger public investments in infrastructure and social sectors; (ii) Improving 
allocative efficiency of resources; (iii) Enacting policy Reforms with a view to 
creating an investor friendly environment; and (iv) Improve governance and enhance the 
efficiency of delivery systems. The details are given in the Tenth Five Year Plan 
document which has been placed before the Parliament. 
194 

[18 August, 2005J RAJYA SABHA 
(c) The Mid-Term Appraisal to the Tenth Five year Plan, as agreed to by the National 
Development Council in its meeting held on 27th -28th June 2005, suggested that it would 
not be possible to achieve the planned rate of growth of 8.1 per cent. The Mid Term 
Appraisal has suggested measures to raise the growth rate in the remaining period of the 
Tenth Plan so as to achieve an overall target of 7 per cent during the plan. The Mid Term 
Appraisal has identified 59 priority areas of action in agriculture, irrigation, rural development, 
watershed development horticulture, fertilizer pricing, food processing, energy, social 
sector/power, rural energy, coal, petroleum, transport, infrastructure, labour and 
employment, industry, governance, etc. The details are available in the Mid-Term

library.

Heavy rains in Mumbai 
2619. SHRI PRAMOD MAHAJAN: Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Meteorological Department failed in pre 
warning the people of Mumbai about likely heavy rains highest in a day in the 
history of India; and 
(b) if so, the steps Government are taking to make weather forecast in India 
more trust worthy? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a ) The Regional Meteorological 
Center, Mumbai initially issued forecast for rather heavy (4-6 cm) to heavy (7-12 
cm) rainfall on 25.7.2005. The same forecast was repeated on 26.7.2005 at 
0600 hrs. (for Akashwani) and 1300 hrs.  (General forecast). The forecast was 
subsequently upgraded to heavy (7-12 cm) to very heavy (above 12 cm) rainfall at 
17.30 hrs. on 26.7.2005. Hon'ble Chief Minister of Maharashtra was apprised of 
the likelyhood of heavy to very heavy rain in a meeting convened by him at 1600 
hrs. on 26.7.2005. 
Actual rainfall recorded up to 1430 hrs. on 26.7.2005 at Santa Cruz was 
only 1.9 cm. however, between 1430 hrs. to 1730 hrs. there was an 
unprecedented steep increase in rainfall and rainfall measurement at Santa Cruz at 
1730 hrs. became 40 cm. which ultimately rose up to 94.4 cm. by 0830 hrs. on 
27.7.2005. This was a highly localized rainfall event confined within a radius of 
about 20-25 km. over central and north Mumbai and took place within a short time 
period. Present level of scientific knowledge of the atmosphere, even at global 
level, cannot predict such localized rainfall 
198 

[18 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
magnitude as on the same day Colaba observatory in South Mumbai recorded 
only about 7.3 cm of rainfall at 0830 hrs. on 27.7.2005.

denser network of observatories and Doppler Radars with capability of 
capturing the small scale details of rain bearing weather systems. These 
observational facilities in conjunction with the advanced regional predictions 
systems that are being developed w ill help in understanding and forecasting 
localized rainfall events.

Revival of sick SSIs 
2645. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will the Minister of SMALL SCALE 
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have formulated any scheme for revival of sick Small 
Scale Industries in the country; 
(b) whether Government propose to give any financial package for revival of 
these industries; and 
(c) if so, the total amount allocated for this purpose by Government during 
the current year? 
THE MINISTER OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES (SHRI MAHAVIR 
PRASAD): (a) The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has circulated in January, 2002 
detailed guidelines on rehabilitation of sick SSI units to all scheduled commercial 
banks for implementation. 
230 

[18 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) and (c) The Union Government does not provide financial assistance to the 
States/Union Territories for rehabilitation of sick SSIs. Financial assistance 
for the rehabilitation of sick SSIs is provided by the primary lending 
institutions (PLIs), including the commercial banks. The Small Industries 
Development Bank of India (SIDBI) has, however, an exclusive Refinance 
Scheme for the PLIs in respect of financial assistance extended by them for 
rehabilitation of sick SSI units. The SIDBI has cumulatively sanctioned and 
disbursed Rs. 62.94 crore and Rs. 32.21 crore respectively to 1,260 sick SSI units 
under the Refinance Scheme for Rehabilitation of Sick SSI Units, as at the end 
of March, 2005. 
Profit of ISRO 
2646. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO: Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the steps Government are taking to capture 10 percent share in the global 
market for launch vehicles and related services; 
(b) the amount that has been earned by ISRO in 2004-05 on providing the 
facility of launching and other related services; and 
(c) the details of countries which have evinced interest in using services of 
CARTOSAT? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER'S OFFICE 
(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN): (a) Indian  launch vehicle programme is 
mainly intended to meet domestic requirements. After meeting internal 
requirements residual capacity is made available for commercial launches for 
other countries. 
The present annual forecast for launch demand globally is about 15-20 
launches into Geostationary orbits and about 3 to 6 launches into other orbits. 
Considering the current market scenario and heavy competition, a maximum of 
5% of the global market share can be ta rgeted by Antrix Corporation Limited 
(Antrix), the marketing arm of ISRO. 
Antrix has been in touch with the potential customers in Europe, Canada, 
Singapore, Indonesia, etc., to offer the launch services. Further, a cooperation 
agreement was also entered into betw een Antrix and Arianespace of France, 
for launch of small as well as larger satellites, by Polar Satellite Launch 
Vehicle (PSLV) and Geosynchronous Satellite 
231 

RAJYASABHA [18 August, 2005] 
Launch Vehicle (GSLV). Promotional efforts are also undertaken through 
participation in appropriate exhibitions from time to time in order to create 
greater awareness of our launch capability among potential customers. 
(b) In 2004-05, ISRO through contracts made by Antrix with foreign 
customers received payments amounting to Rs. 10.54 Crores towards launch 
services on PSLV and Rs. 261 Crores for mission support services; 
(c) USA, Germany, France, Russia, Japan Taiwan, China, Myanmar, 
Algeria, Venezuela, UAE and Sudan have evinced interest in using services 
ofCARTOSAT. 
Bridging the gap between rural and urban areas through 
Satellites 
2647. SHRI RAMA MUNIREDDY SIRIGIREDDY: Will the PRIME 
MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) in what way CARTOSAT, INSAT and EDUSAT are meeting the societal needs 
of the country; 
(b) whether there are any plans before Government to bridge the digital divide 
between the people living in rural areas  and urban areas with the help of 
satellites; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER'S OFFICE 
(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN): (a) CARTOSAT-1 provides data for 
generating three dimensional maps that  help in planning urban and rural 
development, land, water resources mana gement, disaster assessment, relief 
planning and management, INSAT satellites are used for communications, 
broadcasting, meteorological services, disaster management support, Tele-
medicine, Training & Development Communication. EDUSAT provides 
connectivity for schools, colleges higher levels of education to support formal 
and non-formal education including developmental communications. 
(b) and (c) Communication satellites such as INSAT and EDUSAT 
provide the means for bridging the digital divide. Tele-medicine and 
232 

[18 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
Tele-education are two such schemes making use of digital connectivity to reach 
urban facilities to rural areas. Through tele-medicine, high quality medical care is 
being extended to rural and remote areas by transmitting the patient data to the 
specialists in hospitals located in metros and providing video consultancy. The 
services of super specialists are made available to patients in remote parts of the 
country in North East region, central parts of India, Andaman and Nicobar 
Islands, ect. Similarly through tele-educations, high quality education available 
in urban schools and colleges is made accessible to children in remote parts of 
the country, especially in villages.

Farewell to the retiring members 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, on completion of their term of office, some of 
our colleagues are retiring today, the 18th of August. I am happy that three of the 
retiring Members, namely, Shri Ahmed Patel, Shri Abani Roy and Shri 
Chittabrata Majumdar, have already been re-elected. On behalf of the whole 
House and on my own behalf, I bid farewell to the retiring members, namely, 
Shri Lalitbhai Mehta, Shrimati Savita Sharda, Shrimati Chandra Kala Pandey, Shri 
Jibon Roy, Shrimati Sarla Maheshwari, Shri Shankar Roy Chowdhury and Shri 
Eduardo Faleiro who retired on 28th July. 
Hon. Members, the House will surely miss these distinguished Members. As 
Presiding Officer, I shall certainly miss their active participation and the 
liveliness of the speeches they made in this House. I would like to 
249 

RAJYA SABHA [18 August, 2005] 
acknowledge and place on record the valuable contribution they made to the 
proceedings of the House. 
I do hope that the retiring Members also would cherish the happy memory of their 
association with this august House. I am sure they will continue to serve the nation 
with the same vigour and earnestness wherever they may be. I wish them 
Godspeed; may the Almighty always bless them with good health, prosperity 
and happiness. 
THE LEADER OF THE HOUSE (DR. MANMOHAN SINGH): Mr. Chairman, 
Sir, I wish to associate myself with the remarks of appreciation and good wishes 
for the retiring members made by you. We are very happy that three of our 
colleagues, Shri Ahmed Patel, ShriAbani Roy and Shri Chittabrata Majumdar, 
have been re-elected and we look forward to their guidance in the conduct of 
business of this House with renewed pleasure. 
Sir, all the retiring members have distinguished themselves by their 
contribution to the debates in this august House. Ours has been described by my 
great friend, Prof. Amartya Sen, as an argumentative society. And this august 
House, along with the other Hduse, at the apex of our democracy, is changed with the 
responsibility of promoting good governance through processes of argumentation, 
reason, based on sound logic and the quest for truth. 
Our distinguished Members have made a very important contribution to that 
process of carrying forward the dialogue through the instrumentality of Parliament 
and in the process, promoting the cause of good governance of our country. In 
particular, sir, I would like to mention the contribution of Shri Lalitbhai Mehta, a very 
senior, Member of this House. We will miss his scholarly discourses on various 
issues of national interest. Shrimati Savita Sharda made a very important 
contribution and some of the issues that she raised relating to the problems of 
women and other weaker sections, I think, enriched our debate enormously. And, 
who can forget the contribution of Shrimati Chandra Kala Pandey and Shrimati 
Sarla Maheshwari. They are powerful orators by every standard, and whenever 
they participated in our debates, I think, they brought a new perspective to bear on 
the quality of debates, and we will, certainly, miss them. 
Sir, General Roy Chowdhury brought to this House rare experience. He 
250 

[18 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
was the Chief of our Armed Forces and his presence amidst us, I think, brought 
in focus a new dimension of looking at problems of national security, of national 
welfare and how working together we can contribute to finding effective solutions to 
the formidable challenges that our country faces. He represents the best and the 
brightest minds of our country, and I sincerely hope that in the years to come, he 
would be equally productive in contributing to the service of our people. Shri 
Eduardo Faleiro retired on the 28th of July, and, I would like to pay tribute to his 
scholarship; to his concern not only about foreign affairs but also his particular 
concern about the functioning of our secular polity, and to his concern and 
interest in human resource development issues of education, particularly 
higher education. I think, he made a profound impression on all of us. 
Parliament, Sir, is not the only forum, of course, to serve our country. I sinecrely 
hope that the retiring Members will continue to engage themselves because ours is 
not a profession. It is a calling; it is a way of serving our country. And outside 
Parliament also, there are enormous opportunities whereby we can all engage 
ourselves in the service of our country. I take this opportunity, Sir, to wish all the 
retiring Members my very best wishes, and I sincerely hope that some of them, 
at least, will again have an opportunity to come back and return to this House, 
or, the other House. Thank your, Sir.

Demand for Restructuring Civil and Criminal Laws in the Country 
SHRIVIJAY J. DARDA(Maharashtra): Sir, we need to explore ways to 
rejuvenate the administration of justice. The main reason for the Judiciary's 
inability to deliver quick justice is the lack of manpower to clear the gigantic 
backlog of nearly 30 million cases and absence of reforms in the British-
introduced legal system to meet their needs. Of late, people's faith in the 
Judiciary is increasing due to pro-active role being played by courts in matters 
of common interest like lowering the pollution limits, suo moto taking 
cognisance of media-publicised glaring human suffering, either in a solitary 
case or collectively. Thus, cases are increasing, but the number of judges is 
small to handle the workload. Thus, fixing time frame for final disposal should 
be a major determinant factor of any wort hwhile judicial reform. This requires 
increasing the number of judges, fixing time frame and revamping the whole 
procedural laws aiming at reducing delays. The rationale behind still following 
a legal system introduced by the Br itishers, where lawmakers have designed 
the system of cases going on for years to give maximum chance to the 
accused to prove their innocence needs, a fresh look. One suggestion is to 
give more powers to the law-enforcing authority with built-in safeguards so 
that petty cases can be solved at the ground level itself and the burden on the 
Judiciary can also be reduced. The other suggestion is restructuring the 
existing civil and criminal laws keepi ng in view the emerging socio-economic 
ambience, fixing time-frame, streamlini ng the appeal and re-appeal system 
and realistically increasing the number of judges at all levels. Thank you.

Demand for Central Government's Assistance for Developing 
Infrastructural Facilities for Information Technology in Goa 
SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN NAIK (Goa): Sir, while IT revolution is showing 
the possibilities of lifting India out of poverty and leading to overall progress, there 
is a disparity the way this new knowledge revolution is spreading across different 
States, the State of Goa has remained backward in IT revolution. Sir, Goa has a 
good amount of skilled human resources in the IT sector by producing around 
800 engineers and diploma holders every year. However, Goa has not been able 
to attract any of the top Indian IT firms to the State. Given t hat it holds such a 
huge potential for the country, given that it is a non-polluting industry, something 
that is ideally suited to the fragile environment of Goa as well as a major 
source of employment to the youth, it is time that the Government, both Central 
and State, make a concerted effort to bring IT co mpanies to Goa. The Central 
Government should ask the NASSCOM to open its office in Goa. The Central 
Government can give tax benefits to these IT units on a condition of creating a 
definite number of jobs. Good power and broadband connectivity being the lifeline of IT 
companies, both the Central and State Governments should ensure that. With 
initial boost by two Governments, IT industry in Goa will be able to stand on its 
own. Future belongs to those who excel in intellectual work. Today, the world's 
riches man is an IT businessman. Sir, 54 per cent of the Indian population, today, 
is below 25 years of age. So, let us give them a scope. Thank you.

Promotion in the Country 
MS. PRAMILABOHIDAR (Orissa): Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, the Indian farmers, more so, 
the farmers in Orissa, follow the traditional methods of fanning. They largely grow paddy 
both in the Kharif and Rabi seasons. Though paddy is the major produce, it does not fetch a 
good price or profit. Many farmers confine themselves to traditional crops like paddy and that 
leads to distress sales. 
It is, therefore, necessary that they follow crop diversification. The farmers need to 
be educated about the various cash crops. In Orissa, there is enough scope for 
horticulture. Even with small land holdings a farmer can grow cash crops like spices, 
fruits, seasonal vegetables, medicinal and herbal plants. But for this they need 
various inputs. The foremost of them is the "Know-how" and "do-how". The farmers, 
by and large, lack money for investment initially, and orchardry takes time to give the 
returns. Therefore, they have to be financed through soft-loans. 
I understand that Rs.630 crores have been earmarked for the development of 
horticulture. But this is not enough. More funds are required. Research centres and Kisan Talim 
Kendras are required to be set up at block levels, in large numbers, to train farmers in 
Orissa. As a special case, more funds need to be allocated for such activities in Orissa. 
I request the Government, especially, the Minister for Agriculture, to look into this 
matter and provide adequate support for crop diversification and horticultural promotion.

Demand for Legislation to Stop Illegal Inter-Country Adoptions 
SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA(Andhra Pradesh): Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, trade in 
inter-country adoption appears to be a roaring business for the unscrupulous 
agencies in India. These agencies have made India an international baby 
shopping center. In the absence of a legislation to cover ICA, we are only following 
the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court. The problem starts from Voluntary 
Coordinating Agencies in States which are supposed to ensure that children are 
first offered for Indian adoption, and if it fails to happen in 30 days, it will clear 
child for Central Adoption Resource Agency for the ICA. The point is, there are a 
number of loopholes in the Supreme Court's guidelines and, taking advantage of 
this, private adoption agencies are doing business with infants and children. The 
ICA is primarily and ad hoc humanitarian response to children who are 
orphaned. Private adoption agencies have kept this spirit at the backburner and are 
using abusive, illegal, unethical and clandestine methods such as abduction of 
babies, identifying vulnerable mothers, falsely imforming biological mother that 
her baby is stillborn or dead, buying ch ildren from poor families and also by 
producing fake letters, and are getting children for the ICA. This came to light in 
1999 in States like Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Delhi, etc. Immediately, in 
2000, the Andhra Pradesh Government barred voluntary agencies from placing 
children in adoption. Andhra Pradesh is the first and the only State to have 
prohibited this, looking at the abuse of spirit behind the ICA, and the State itself has 
taken over adoption process. 
So, to plug loopholes in guidelines and in the absence of legislation with 
regard to adoption, I request the Government of India to have a 
comprehensive legislation on the ICA of children.'

Sir, the most unfortunate state of affairs is the poor condition of health in the rural areas. 
There are hospitals, but no doctors are going there. It is found that when posted in the

the urban areas. Last week, one of my friends, Shri Jothi, was saying that such laws

Sir, it is a fact that medical colleges are being opened. There are Government

be a scheme, a system like the Border Security Force—wherein BSF personnel are

a special recruitment for rural areas health care unit. If the service is meant for the
